findings.title: Build the large SQLite ID list without repeated string copies
findings.body: When the configured batch size exceeds SQLite’s parameter limit, this loop rebuilds the entire accumulated SQL fragment for every ID. With the 32,767-ID batch covered by the new test, it copies several gigabytes of string data and creates substantial garbage for one delete. Use a builder or join the IDs so construction is linear in the batch size.

findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: This logs at error level for every normal batch, including the full list of annotation IDs; the corresponding completion logs do the same. Routine cleanup will therefore produce error-level noise and potentially large log volume, making real failures harder to find. These messages should use an appropriate non-error level and avoid logging the full ID list.

findings.title: Run every cleanup job ten times more frequently
findings.body: Changing the shared cleanup ticker from ten minutes to one minute causes all cleanup jobs in this service—not just annotation cleanup—to run up to ten times as often. This increases recurring database and filesystem work; if a run takes longer than a minute, the buffered ticker can also trigger another run immediately afterward. Keep the prior interval or change the scheduling of annotation cleanup specifically if it needs a higher frequency.
